question: A urine culture grows E. coli with the AST report: Cefotaxime MIC 32 µg/mL (R), Meropenem MIC 0.25 µg/mL (S), ESBL detected. The treating clinician wants to continue cefotaxime because 'the patient was responding clinically.' What is the correct microbiological advice?

answers.text: Advise against cefotaxime — CLSI mandates all cephalosporins be reported Resistant for ESBL producers regardless of in vitro MIC, as clinical failure is documented

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. ESBL-producing Enterobacterales exhibit an inoculum effect: in vitro MICs may appear low, but in vivo drug concentrations at the infection site are insufficient, leading to clinical failure. CLSI/EUCAST interpretive rules override raw MIC values for ESBL producers.

answers.text: Agree with the clinician — MIC 32 µg/mL is achievable with high-dose cefotaxime in urine

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Even though urinary drug concentrations can be high, the inoculum effect in ESBL producers means cephalosporin MICs underestimate true resistance. CLSI rules explicitly override in vitro MIC for ESBL-positive isolates.

answers.text: Request repeat culture — the ESBL result may be a laboratory error

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. ESBL detection uses validated phenotypic confirmatory tests (e.g. clavulanate synergy). Requesting a repeat solely to challenge a confirmed ESBL result delays appropriate therapy.

answers.text: Suggest adding clavulanate to the cefotaxime to overcome the ESBL

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Cefotaxime–clavulanate is not a licensed or validated combination. While beta-lactamase inhibitors can overcome some ESBLs in vitro, this strategy is clinically unreliable and not recommended by any guideline.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the CLSI/EUCAST interpretive rules for ESBL producers: all penicillins, cephalosporins, and aztreonam must be reported as Resistant regardless of in vitro MIC.
Well done. Interpreting AST reports for ESBL producers requires applying CLSI interpretive rules, not just reading raw MIC values.
